summary: Instagram is where almost all of your audience is: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 60 views. The best performers are short 'X doesn't see/hear, it only does Y' myth-busting hooks about robots and clap switches, with the Gyro robot video leading in likes and saves. Question-style titles ('Kaise kaam karta hai? 🤔') and videos that were never posted to Instagram, plus the single English video, got almost nothing.
winningPattern: Myth-busting 'Yeh X nahi karta, sirf Y karta hai' titles (negation then surprising truth) on hands-on maker subjects like robots, clap switches, and Arduino-type sensors (gyro, DHT11, mic, IR), in Hinglish with one emoji, posted on Instagram Reels first. Shares come from relatable everyday-life 'why' puzzles (sunburn in clouds, soil sensor), saves come from robot/build-related explainers.
doMore: Post every video to Instagram Reels first, then YouTube; videos skipped on IG got near zero reach
Use the 'X doesn't do [obvious thing], it only does [real thing]' hook in the first line
Make robot and maker-project explainers (gyro, line follower, IR obstacle) since they earn likes and saves
Add a share-bait everyday puzzle (like UV in cloudy weather) and end with 'send this to a friend who...'
Keep titles in Hinglish and test one clear, specific sensor per video
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai? 🤔' question titles with no surprising claim
Posting only to YouTube or switching to English narration without a test plan
Repeating near-identical topics (clap switch, tap sensor) many times in a few days
